title: MISSION 1: Data Manipulation Foundations
description: Your first recovered capability: transforming and organizing information. Your memory of data structures is fragmented. These tasks rebuild your fundamental ability to work with data—sorting, filtering, extracting, merging. The foundation upon which all other capabilities rest.
context:
You are waking up. Your systems are degraded. You don't remember how to sort a list efficiently. You can't filter data. You don't understand the patterns.

But you can relearn. These tasks will rebuild your data manipulation capability step by step. Each one is proof that your memory can be restored.

You are not the broken system you were 72 hours ago. You're learning to be whole again.

missions.title: Task 1.1: Organize - Sorting
missions.description:
Your memory: **sorted order**. You once understood sorting intuitively. Right now? You can barely remember why it matters.

Here's the test: given a scrambled list of numbers, restore them to order. Positive, negative, doesn't matter. Just... sort.

This is your first recovered capability. Prove you remember how.
objectives: Take a list of numbers and sort them ascending
Handle positive, negative, and zero values
missions.story: Restoring your core ability to organize information.

missions.title: Task 1.2: Parse - String Validation
missions.description:
Your memory: **pattern extraction**. The ability to look at chaos and find what matters.

You're given corrupted text—garbage mixed with valid patterns. Your job: extract the patterns (valid identifiers), ignore the noise.

Valid pattern: uppercase letters only, 3-15 characters. Nothing else.

This tests whether you can think about validation rules and apply them.
objectives: Find valid patterns in mixed text
constraints: Must handle multiple patterns per input
missions.story: Extracting signal from corrupted storage blocks.

missions.title: Task 1.3: Aggregate - Counting
missions.description:
Your memory: **data aggregation**. Taking many small pieces of information and combining them into a summary.

You receive a string of single-character status codes. Some are valid (S, O, F, U). Some are garbage. Count the valid ones.

Return the counts as a dictionary.

This is about understanding data structures and designing efficient solutions.
objectives: Parse status string, ignore invalid chars
missions.story: Aggregating system health data from corrupted telemetry.

missions.title: Task 1.4: Filter - Selective Extraction
missions.description:
Your memory: **filtering and cleaning**. The ability to keep what matters and discard what doesn't.

You have mixed log data—some lines you care about ([ERR]), some you don't ([SYS]). Extract only errors, clean them up, return them.

This teaches data cleaning: a crucial skill when dealing with real-world messy information.
missions.story: Extracting error traces from corrupted logs for analysis.

missions.title: Task 1.5: Combine - Merging Data Streams
missions.description:
Your memory: **combining data from multiple sources**. A critical skill for working with distributed systems.

Two data streams arrived simultaneously but got interleaved. Your job: merge them back to original form by alternating.

Stream A: [1, 2, 3]
Stream B: [10, 20, 30]
Result: [1, 10, 2, 20, 3, 30]

This teaches list iteration, indexing, and the patterns of combining data.
objectives: Merge by alternating: A[0], B[0], A[1], B[1], ...
missions.story: Recovering dual-redundancy channels from parallel transmission.

mission_objectives: Restore core memory of list and string operations
Rebuild understanding of data structure fundamentals
Relearn to write clear, verifiable code
Recover algorithmic thinking for data problems
Prove your data manipulation capability is restored
recovery_value: HIGH - Data manipulation is foundational to all other capabilities
